item.title: Airbus plane from Dublin to Rome diverted to France after bomb alert
item.description: The situation is being monitored, a statement from French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s office said.

item.title: ‘It would destroy the Democrat Party’: Trump dismisses impeachment threat
item.description: US President Donald Trump has warned that impeaching him would damage the Democratic Party, after Republicans suffered major losses in the midterm elections.

item.title: NASA astronauts cast US election votes from the International Space Station
item.description: In a rare event, three American astronauts voted in Tuesday's US midterm elections from the International Space Station, using advanced links to send electronic ballots to officials on Earth.

item.title: 'Cautious optimism' for renewed US engagement on climate as delegation heads to COP31
item.description: Delegation members plan to "explore opportunities for renewed US engagement on climate, energy, and economic policy" at the UN summit.

item.title: Americans 'stay optimists', 'tremendous growth' in AI to continue, says US-EU wealth manager Xavier Volatier
item.description: Xavier Volatier, head of Transatlantic Private Wealth, speaks to our Stefan Grobe on the effects of the US mid-terms' result on the global markets.

item.title: Supermarket freezer cyberattack 'not sophisticated,' Prof. Kevin Curran explains
item.description: Stefan Grobe speaks to Kevin Curran, Professor of Cybersecurity at the University of Ulster. He explains that the attack was 'not sophisticated', and vulnerabilities were known long term.

item.title: Change in Texas could 'shape the US presidential election', says analyst Eric Ham
item.description: Eric Ham, US political analyst, said that US Democrats believe that many African-American, Latino and young voters are again "up for grabs" after they gave their support for Trump in past presidential elections.

item.title: Gaza: Displaced Palestinian builds wind turbine to generate electricity
item.description: A displaced Palestinian in Gaza has built a makeshift wind turbine to bring electricity to tents in Khan Younis. Unable to afford solar panels, he has found a way to harness the wind to power everyday essentials.

item.title: Oil giants cash in on the US-Iran conflict. Can an EU-wide tax on oil profits ease the energy crisis?
item.description: A new report commissioned by Greenpeace Germany found that oil companies earned €36 billion in additional margins from the fallout of the US-Iran conflict between March 1 and October 19. Can Europe tax these profits to help ease rising energy bills?

item.title: Iran is a 'wounded animal' and will 'seek revenge', Pahlavi says
item.description: Reza Pahlavi, son of the former Shah of Iran, thinks the Iranian regime is "willing to go all the way for its own survival".

item.title: Emmanuel Macron's frank Telegram messages revealed in Françoise Degois' new book
item.description: Françoise Degois publishes "You are all too hard on me", a book in which she records her private exchanges with the president.

item.title: 'Imposter': Why is the Chucky creator angry with Nicki Minaj?
item.description: The American rapper, who has been an outspoken supporter of Donald Trump, posted a seemingly AI-generated version of the famous killer doll in a MAGA election day post. This did not sit well with Don Mancini, Chucky's creator.

item.title: Europe weighs implications of Trump’s midterm setback
item.description: Good morning. It’s Thursday, and I’m Mared Gwyn. In this edition: What the Democrats’ sweeping win in the US midterm elections means for Europe, and Germany and Brussels continue to clash over what "associate" EU membership actually means.

item.title: US First Lady Melania Trump to host Ukrainian and Russian officials at White House
item.description: On Wednesday, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy awarded the first lady a national honour for her role in brokering a partial ceasefire that allowed the evacuation of civilians from a Russian-occupied town.

item.title: New Zealand: Dead whales found as rescuers battle mass stranding
item.description: Volunteers in New Zealand are working to save pilot whales stranded along the Wairarapa coast, near Cape Palliser. At least 14 have been helped back into the water, but many others have died along the remote coastline.

item.title: ‘Zeptoverse’: CERN scientists uncover evidence of extraordinarily rare particle decay
item.description: Scientists at CERN have found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay using the Large Hadron Collider. The process is predicted to occur just once in every 10 billion cases, offering researchers a new way to explore the subatomic world.

item.title: Europe Today: Trump loses Congress. Will he now be even more unpredictable?
item.description: Democrats have seized control of the US Congress in a nationwide rejection of Trump. In Europe, hackers targeted a French blood bank and supermarket fridges, raising fears of a new front in hybrid warfare. Plus: we talk to Reza Pahlavi, one of the main leaders of the opposition to the Tehran regime.

item.title: Ban it or build it? Europe considers how to regulate social media
item.description: France’s under-15 social media ban has already fallen in court, and Australia’s is now on trial. Meanwhile, a new European coalition is betting on a different fix: build better platforms.

item.title: Crises have taken their classrooms. But education cannot wait
item.description: "Today, the education of 258 million school-aged children worldwide is disrupted by crises," says Reem Alabali Radovan, Germany's Minister for Development in an exclusive op-ed for Euronews. That is why Germany is providing €20 million in funding for education in emergencies over the coming years.

item.title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 more years for collusion
item.description: Wong rose to prominence during Hong Kong's 2014 protests, known as the Umbrella Movement, and has been in and out of jail since 2017.

item.title: Seven decades behind the lens: Ghana's James Barnor receives top photography honour
item.description: From his studio in Accra to the pages of "Drum" magazine, Barnor documented everyday life and Black culture during a period of profound social change.

item.title: Arab airlines set to record a collective net loss of €3.82 billion in 2026, AACO report reveals
item.description: At its AGM held this week in Doha, the Arab Air Carriers’ Organization raised concerns over EU carbon regulations, as airlines look to boost European connectivity amid ongoing regional uncertainty.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 5th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 5th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Food prices in Europe: Where are grocery costs rising fastest?
item.description: Food price rises in Europe have been modest this year, but fresh produce is getting pricier, with prices up 8% in France and supply disruptions leaving shelves empty in southern Italy.

item.title: Tech companies hit by new AI worries on positive day for most markets
item.description: Apart from tech stocks, shares mostly gained on Thursday after Wall Street rallied following the midterm elections, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumping more than 3% after President Donald Trump’s party lost its sole control of Washington.

item.title: Block 10: new German film brings Auschwitz experiments on women to the screen
item.description: A little-known Auschwitz block where hundreds of Jewish women were used as test subjects is now a film by Berlin producer Alice Brauner, who tells Euronews of tearful shoots and renewed anger.

item.title: What teeth from a centuries-old cemetery can teach us about climate shocks and disease
item.description: Scientists say that climate shocks may have been ‘overlooked’ when researching certain diseases in the Industrial Revolution.

item.title: Serbia arrests police over excessive violence against student protesters
item.description: The police officers are accused of having used excessive force and violence against student protesters during anti-government protests last year.

item.title: As tiger mosquitoes spread, Europe races to stop tropical diseases
item.description: Mosquitoes that were associated with tropical regions are now established in several European countries and are moving north. Health authorities are rushing to ensure that the diseases they spread — such as dengue, chikungunya and Zika — don’t catch up with them. And citizens have an important role.

item.title: Spain: Madrid hosts 30th Ibero-American Summit with 22-nation bloc
item.description: Spain is hosting the 30th Ibero-American Summit in Madrid, bringing together leaders from Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking nations. The gathering aims to strengthen cooperation across Europe and Latin America.

item.title: Zelenskyy makes surprise visit to Madrid for talks with Sánchez and Latin American leaders
item.description: Zelenskyy visits Madrid to meet Sánchez, Felipe VI and Latin American leaders at the Ibero-American Summit, aiming to boost support for Ukraine and closer ties with Latin America.

item.title: Indra to lead Spanish alliance guarding Europe's undersea infrastructure
item.description: The project will combine sovereign AI, advanced sensors and unmanned vehicles to constantly monitor the water mass from surface to seabed, making national industry a European security benchmark.

item.title: Hungary: communist-era files released, up to 60,000 former agents revealed
item.description: Hungary released communist-era secret police files Wednesday, identifying up to 60,000 informants, a path for Hungary in reckoning with its repressive past.

item.title: Euronews chairman supports 'Gibraltar model' to bring Western Balkan nations into Schengen
item.description: Euronews held an EU Enlargement Summit in Brussels on Tuesday, hosting policymakers and political leaders from candidate countries to discuss how the next phase of the European Union's enlargement can be imagined.

item.title: MEPs debate EU enlargement at Euronews Summit in Brussels
item.description: As the European Commission released its latest progress report on candidate countries, MEPs Riho Terras (EPP) and Pasquale Tridico (The Left Group) go head to head over one of Europe's most ambitious political projects.

item.title: Bob Dylan meets Pope Leo XIV in the Vatican, with music, faith and a rosary gift
item.description: Bob Dylan meets Pope Leo XIV in the Vatican. The Pontiff gives him a rosary, the Nobel laureate gives him his autobiography. Tomorrow, the concert in Rome.

item.title: Brazil: Santa Claus School celebrates graduation at Christ the Redeemer
item.description: Dozens of Santas gathered at Rio de Janeiro's iconic Christ the Redeemer statue to celebrate their graduation. The 55 new recruits are preparing to spread Christmas cheer across Brazil.

item.title: Just six climate actions could save 1.6 million lives a year, WHO says
item.description: The WHO is urging governments to scale up six measures to tackle the health impacts of climate change, saying they could save millions of lives while delivering major economic benefits.

item.title: As maritime threats grow, France pushes to strengthen Europe's naval power
item.description: France is at the forefront of efforts to strengthen Europe's naval capabilities. Its growing naval arsenal is on display this week at Euronaval, the world's largest naval defence show, held annually near Paris.

item.title: WHO backs trials for two new vaccines against Ebola outbreak
item.description: The vaccine trials could offer new hope in the fight against an outbreak caused by an Ebola strain with no approved vaccine.

item.title: Grand Voyager in Copenhagen: cycling, culture and Nordic cuisine
item.description: Copenhagen, Denmark’s capital, is known for its colourful architecture, rich cultural heritage and relaxed way of life. It’s a city where historic landmarks and modern Scandinavian design sit together. One of the best ways to discover the city is with a local guide. In this episode of Grand Voyager,

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 4th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 4th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: UK: Police arrest Palestine Action supporters outside Supreme Court
item.description: Police arrested supporters of Palestine Action outside the Supreme Court in London, United Kingdom, on Wednesday 4 November, as a legal battle over the British government's ban on the group resumed.

item.title: UK parliament risks 'catastrophic failure' after renovation delay
item.description: The Palace of Westminster could risk severe damage as the ageing building's renovation has been continuously postponed over political disagreements.

item.title: Ukraine: Police footage captures Russian strike on Komyshuvakha shelter
item.description: Bodycam footage from a police officer killed in the attack captures the moments before a Russian bomb strikes a shelter in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 37 people.

item.title: Goncourt 2026 winner Philippe Jaenada admits using AI in novel to 'play with reader'
item.description: A day after being crowned with France's top literary award, Philippe Jaenada, spoke on France Inter radio about how he used AI to write "The Unknown Woman from Quai de Javel", the novel that won him this year's Goncourt Prize.

item.title: ‘Everything is on the table’: EU to discuss new measures against Georgia in January, Kallas says
item.description: EU foreign ministers will hold a “deep dive” in January on new measures against Georgia, Kallas said, as the European Commission's annual report flags deepening backsliding in democratic standards.

item.title: Armenia sees 'totally new global role' for South Caucasus 'as a whole'
item.description: Armenia’s Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told Euronews that peace and convergence in the South Caucasus, based on a carefully balanced pro-EU political vector, create a major opportunity for the region, with "democracy as a strategy" for Armenia.

item.title: Euronews Summit in Brussels: "Let's enlarge Europe. Now."
item.description: "Citizens of the candidate countries are Europeans, in their hearts but also in their minds. Let us complete and reunite the continent" said Pedro Vargas David, Chairman of Euronews, at the Euronews Enlargement Summit in Brussels, addressing high-profile guests, including numerous heads of state.

item.title: Danish youth join European-wide protests against education cuts
item.description: Government plans to cut student allowances has drawn thousands of Danes to the streets on Wednesday, adding to a wave of European youth anger. The bill aims to cut or lower state grants to students whose parents have a medium-to-high income.
